rule-email-legacy-unavailable: Kon nie die reël-e-posse wat op hersiening wag, laai nie. Verfris om weer te probeer.
rule-email-legacy-access-denied: Die reël se outeur het nie meer toegang tot hierdie kaart nie, of die reël het verander, dus kan dit nie weer gekoppel word nie. Jy kan dit weggooi.
rule-email-legacy-source-changed: Die aktiwiteit wat hierdie e-pos geaktiveer het, het verander, dus kan dit nie weer gekoppel word nie. Jy kan dit weggooi.
rule-email-legacy-source-unavailable: Die kaart waaruit hierdie e-pos ontstaan het, is nie meer beskikbaar nie, dus kan dit nie weer gekoppel word nie. Jy kan dit weggooi.
rule-email-legacy-plan-unavailable: Die reëluitvoering wat hierdie e-pos voorberei het, word nie meer gestoor nie, dus kan dit nie weer gekoppel word nie. Jy kan dit weggooi.
rule-email-legacy-attempt-exists: Hierdie e-pos is reeds gestuur, daar is reeds probeer om dit te stuur, of dit is weggegooi.
rule-email-legacy-not-legacy: Hierdie e-pos is reeds weer gekoppel.
rule-email-legacy-failed: Kon nie hierdie handeling voltooi nie. Verfris en probeer weer.
stuck-sync-operation-heading: Lyssinchronisasiebewerkings wat nie hervat kan word nie
stuck-sync-operation-description: Elkeen van hierdie gestoorde lyssinchronisasiebewerkings het halfpad gestop en kan nie meer voltooi word nie, omdat die lys verwyder, herskep of herkonfigureer is, of omdat die gebruiker wat dit begin het skryftoegang verloor het. Terwyl so 'n bewerking wag, kan daardie lys nie sinchroniseer nie. Gooi dit weg sodat die lys weer kan sinchroniseer: veranderinge wat reeds toegepas is, bly behoue, die oorblywende gestoorde veranderinge word nooit geskryf nie, en die volgende sinchronisasie vergelyk die lys weer met sy bron.
stuck-sync-operation-reason-scope-change: Die lys is verwyder, herskep of sy sinchronisasie-instellings is verander
stuck-sync-operation-reason-access-denie: Die gebruiker wat dit begin het, het nie meer skryftoegang tot die hele lys nie
stuck-sync-operation-reason-trigger-unkn: Deur 'n vroeëre WeKan-weergawe gestoor sonder inligting oor wat dit begin het
stuck-sync-operation-reason-intent-missi: Die rekord van wie dit begin het, ontbreek
stuck-sync-operation-reason-unknown: Kon nie nou nagegaan word nie
stuck-sync-operation-replayable-now: Dit kan nou weer hervat word en sal vanself voltooi, daarom kan dit nie weggegooi word nie.
stuck-sync-operation-discard-confirm: Gooi hierdie gestoorde lyssinchronisasiebewerking weg? Veranderinge wat reeds toegepas is, bly behoue; die res word nooit geskryf nie. Die lys kan daarna weer sinchroniseer.
stuck-sync-operation-empty: Geen lyssinchronisasiebewerkings wag vir hersiening nie.
stuck-sync-operation-truncated: Slegs die 50 oudste bewerkings word gewys. Gooi sommige weg en verfris om meer te sien.
stuck-sync-operation-unavailable: Kon nie die lyssinchronisasiebewerkings laai nie. Verfris om weer te probeer.
stuck-sync-operation-missing: Hierdie bewerking is nie meer hangende nie.
stuck-sync-operation-not-stuck: Daar is nie vasgestel dat hierdie bewerking vasgesteek het nie, daarom kan dit nie weggegooi word nie.
stuck-sync-operation-replayable: Hierdie bewerking kan nou weer hervat word en sal vanself voltooi, daarom is dit nie weggegooi nie.
stuck-sync-operation-busy: Hierdie lys sinchroniseer tans. Probeer oor 'n oomblik weer.
stuck-sync-operation-failed: Kon nie hierdie aksie voltooi nie. Verfris en probeer weer.
interrupted-import-heading: Raadinvoere wat voor voltooiing gestop het
interrupted-import-description: Elkeen van hierdie raadinvoere het halfpad gestop — die bediener het herbegin of die invoer het misluk — en 'n gedeeltelike raad agtergelaat. 'n Invoer kan nie voortgesit word nie, omdat die bronlêer nie bewaar word nie. Behou die raad soos dit is, of gooi dit weg en voer die lêer weer in. Weggooi verwyder die raad wat hierdie invoer geskep het en alles daarop, insluitend enigiets wat sedertdien bygevoeg is.
interrupted-import-state-discarding: Word weggegooi; gooi weer weg om te voltooi
interrupted-import-scrum: Die Scrum-fase het sy eie kontrolepunt (__state__, __next__ van __total__ stappe). As jy die raad behou, voltooi of gooi daardie fase weg via die raad se Scrum-invoerherstel.
interrupted-import-counts: __swimlanes__ swembane, __lists__ lyste, __cards__ kaarte, __checklists__ kontrolelyste, __comments__ opmerkings, __attachments__ aanhegsels
interrupted-import-keep-confirm: Behou hierdie gedeeltelike raad soos dit is? Niks word verwyder nie, en die invoer word nie meer hier gelys nie.
interrupted-import-discard-confirm: Gooi hierdie invoer weg? Die raad wat dit geskep het en alles daarop word permanent verwyder.
interrupted-import-empty: Geen onderbroke raadinvoere wag vir hersiening nie.
interrupted-import-truncated: Slegs die 50 oudste invoere word gewys. Behou of gooi sommige weg en verfris om meer te sien.
interrupted-import-unavailable: Kon nie die onderbroke raadinvoere laai nie. Verfris om weer te probeer.
interrupted-import-missing: Hierdie invoer is nie meer aangeteken nie.
interrupted-import-not-interrupted: Hierdie invoer wag nie meer op 'n besluit nie.
interrupted-import-foreign-board: Die raad met hierdie ID is nie deur hierdie invoer geskep nie en is dus nie verander nie.
interrupted-import-scrum-busy: Die Scrum-fase word nog geskryf of herstel. Probeer oor 'n paar minute weer.
interrupted-import-failed: Kon nie hierdie aksie voltooi nie. Verfris en probeer weer.
saml-login-not-started: Hierdie SAML-aanmelding is nie in hierdie blaaieroortjie begin nie. Meld asseblief weer aan.
history-request-pending-undo: Jou laaste ongedaanmaking is nog nie deur die bediener bevestig nie.
history-request-pending-redo: Jou laaste herdoening is nog nie deur die bediener bevestig nie.
history-request-hint: Om weer te probeer herhaal dieselfde versoek, dus kan dit nooit 'n tweede verandering ongedaan maak nie.
scrum-history-checkpoint-stuck: 'n Ontdoen, herdoen of herstel van Scrum-veranderinge het weens 'n konflik gestop. Scrum-wysigings op hierdie raad word geblokkeer totdat dit opgelos is.
scrum-history-checkpoint-counts: __applied__ van __total__ veranderinge is geskryf, __pending__ is nie geskryf nie, en __conflicted__ is sedertdien deur iemand anders verander.
scrum-history-checkpoint-hint: Terugrol plaas elke veranderde rekord terug soos dit voorheen was; dit is slegs beskikbaar wanneer niemand anders daardie rekords sedertdien verander het nie. Om die raad te behou soos dit is, verwyder die gestopte bewerking en verander geen rekords nie. Albei keuses word onder Administrasiepaneel, Probleme, Herstel aangeteken.
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard: Behou die raad soos dit is
scrum-history-checkpoint-discard-confirm: Behou elke rekord soos dit nou is, insluitend die veranderinge wat die gestopte bewerking reeds geskryf het?
scrum-history-checkpoint-ask-admin: 'n Raadsadministrateur kan dit terugrol of die raad behou soos dit is.
login-setting-clear-secret: Verwyder die waarde wat in die administrasiepaneel gestoor is
login-setting-after-restart: Tree in werking nadat WeKan herbegin is
login-setting-env-only: Slegs die bedieneromgewing stel hierdie waardes. Hulle word hier as leesalleen gewys.
email-to-card-description: 'n E-pos wat na jou raad se adres gestuur word, word 'n kaart op daardie raad.
email-to-card-webhook: Inkomende webhook-URL van die e-posverskaffer (Mailgun, SendGrid, Postmark of 'n rou MIME-aanstuurder)
email-to-card-secret-saved: Gestoor - laat leeg om dit te behou
email-to-card-sandstorm-board: Raad waarheen e-pos aan hierdie grein gaan
email-to-card-sandstorm-board-none: Geen - slegs e-posse met 'n raadtoken in die onderwerp
email-to-card-sandstorm-subject: Sit dit in die onderwerp om hierdie raad as jouself te bereik:
email-to-card-parts: Dele van 'n e-pos om te gebruik
email-to-card-address-private: Hou dit privaat: enigiemand wat dit het, kan kaarte as jy byvoeg.
email-to-card-new-address: Nuwe adres (die ou een werk nie meer nie)
email-to-card-off-admin-off: Ontvangs van e-pos is nie in die Admin Paneel opgestel nie.
email-to-card-off-board-off: 'n Raadadministrateur het nie e-pos vir hierdie raad aangeskakel nie.
email-to-card-off-member-off: Jy het jou raadadresse in Lid-instellings afgeskakel.
email-to-card-off-sandstorm-no-session: Die grein het nog nie sy e-posadres nie. Herlaai die bladsy.
email-to-card-off-not-authorized: Jy het skryftoegang tot hierdie raad nodig.
inbound-domain-invalid: Dit is nie 'n geldige domeinnaam nie.
inbound-domain-required: Gee die domein van die raadadresse.
feature-views-email-desc: Die raad as 'n posbus: die e-poslys is die Inkassie, lyste is vouers, etikette is etikette, en lede skryf en beantwoord e-pos vanaf die raad se adres.
email-view-not-receiving: Hierdie raad ontvang nog nie e-pos nie. Skakel dit aan in die raad se Kennisgewinginstellings → E-pos na kaart.
email-view-invalid-address: Een van die adresse is nie 'n geldige e-posadres nie.
email-view-no-recipient: Voeg ten minste een ontvanger by.
email-view-too-many: Te veel e-posse in die afgelope uur gestuur. Probeer later weer.
email-view-no-list: Die raad het 'n lys vir die e-pos nodig.
email-view-send-failed: Die e-pos kon nie gestuur word nie.
feature-views-chat-desc: Die raad as 'n kletswerkspasie: werkspasies, borde, swembane, lyste en kaarte as 'n boom van kanale, die kaart in die middel en sy kommentaar as kletsboodskappe.
chat-view-resize: Sleep om die grootte te verander
chat-view-pick-card: Kies 'n kaart uit die kanale om dit hier te sien.
chat-view-no-messages: Nog geen boodskappe nie. Skryf die eerste een.
feature-views-column-sets-desc: Dieselfde kaarte in verskeie benoemde stelle kolomme - volgens voltooiing, prioriteit, mylpaal of enigiets anders - tussen kolomme geskuif deur te sleep.
feature-rule-suggestions-desc: Bordkieslys → Reëls stel reëls voor uit wat mense op die bord gereeld met die hand doen.
feature-board-summary-desc: Bordkieslys → Opsomming wys wat elke persoon die laaste dag of week op die bord gedoen het, en wat agterstallig is.
feature-since-last-visit-desc: Bordkieslys → Sedert jou laaste besoek wys wat ander op die bord verander het sedert jy dit laas oop gehad het.
feature-search-phrases-desc: Globale soektog verstaan gewone frases soos "my agterstallige kaarte" en maak dit operateurs.
column-sets-empty: Nog geen kolomstelle nie. 'n Raadadministrateur kan een maak: gee dit 'n naam en voeg dan sy kolomme by.
feature-views-version-control-desc: Die bord as 'n GitHub- of Gitea-kwessiespoorder: kaarte as kwessies, etikette en mylpale, kommentaar as die gesprek, aanhangsels as lêers, en die bordgeskiedenis met ongedaanmaak.
vcs-no-issues: Geen kwessies pas by hierdie soektog nie.
vcs-no-milestones: Nog geen mylpale nie. 'n Etiket met 'n sperdatum is 'n mylpaal.
vcs-no-list: Hierdie bord het geen lys of baan vir die kwessie nie.
card-qr-code-desc: Skandeer dit om hierdie kaart op 'n foon of tablet oop te maak.
card-qr-code-too-long: Die skakel van hierdie kaart is te lank vir 'n QR-kode.
vcs-no-wiki: Nog geen wiki nie. Die GitHub-organisasie-invoer bring 'n bewaarplek se wiki hierheen.
github-org-import-desc: Elke bewaarplek van 'n organisasie of 'n gebruiker word sy eie bord, oopgemaak in Board View / Version Control: sy kwessies met hul kommentaar, etikette en lêers, sy vrystellings, sy GitHub Actions-werkvloeie as Reëls, en sy wiki.
github-org-import-token-hint: Nodig vir private bewaarplekke en 'n hoër API-limiet. Dit word slegs gebruik terwyl die invoer loop en word nooit gestoor nie.
github-org-import-issues: Kwessies, met kommentaar, etikette en lêers
github-org-import-owner-invalid: Skryf 'n organisasie- of gebruikersnaam, of sy GitHub-adres.
github-org-import-no-repos: Geen bewaarplekke om in te voer nie.
optional-apis-desc: REST API's in die vorm van ander opspoorders se API's, sodat hulle toepassings en skripte hierdie WeKan as hul agterkant kan gebruik: wat hulle stoor, word in WeKan gestoor, op WeKan-borde. Elkeen is af totdat dit hier gemerk word. Geeneen het eie regte nie: 'n kliënt meld aan met 'n WeKan API-token en kan net sien en verander wat daardie persoon in WeKan kan sien en verander. Almal vereis dat die WeKan REST API aan is (WITH_API=true). Die adres onder elkeen is wat 'n kliënt as sy bediener gebruik.
optional-api-trello-desc: Toepassings en skripte wat vir Trello se REST API geskryf is (byvoorbeeld Trellinator), werk met WeKan: borde, lyste, kaarte, etikette, lede, kommentaar en kontrolelyste. Die Trello-token is 'n WeKan API-token. Om 'n kaart te skrap, argiveer dit in WeKan.
optional-api-jira-desc: Kliënte van Jira se REST API v2 werk met WeKan: 'n projek is 'n bord (sy sleutel is die bordsleutel), 'n kwessie is 'n kaart (DEV-7), 'n status is 'n lys, en 'n oorgang skuif die kaart. Soek aanvaar eenvoudige JQL: project, status, assignee = currentUser(), text en ORDER BY. Meld aan met 'n WeKan API-token as die wagwoord. Om 'n kwessie te skrap, argiveer dit.
optional-api-github-desc: Kliënte van GitHub se REST API vir kwessies werk met WeKan: 'n bewaarplek is 'n bord, 'n kwessie is 'n kaart, met etikette, mylpale (etikette met 'n sperdatum), kommentaar, en oop of gesluit soos in Bordaansig / Weergawebeheer. Die token is 'n WeKan API-token.
optional-api-gitea-desc: Kliënte van Gitea en Forgejo se REST API vir kwessies werk met WeKan, op dieselfde manier as die GitHub-versoenbare API: 'n bewaarplek is 'n bord en 'n kwessie is 'n kaart. Die token is 'n WeKan API-token.
bots-none: Nog geen robotte nie. 'n Robot is 'n uitvoerder op jou eie bediener - 'n KI-agent, 'n CI-taak, 'n skrip - waaraan hierdie raad kaarte oorhandig.
bot-not-found: Daardie robot is nie op hierdie raad nie.
bot-option-not-found: Daardie antwoord is nie een wat die robot aangebied het nie.
webhook-internal-hosts-desc: Uitgaande webhooks mag nie adresse op WeKan se eie netwerk bereik nie, sodat niemand 'n raad se webhook na 'n interne diens kan rig nie. Lys hier die gashere op daardie netwerk wat webhooks mag bereik - 'n Node-RED, 'n kletsbediener - een per reël, as 'n naam of 'n adres, met 'n poort om slegs daardie poort toe te laat. Leeg: geen. Slegs werfadministrateurs kan hierdie lys verander.
account-webhook-desc: Een adres wat WeKan inlig wanneer iemand aanmeld of 'n nuwe rekening geskep word. Niks word gestuur totdat 'n gebeurtenis hieronder gemerk is nie. Dit dra die gebeurtenis, die gebruikersnaam en die tyd; merk meer velde net as die ontvanger dit nodig het.
account-webhook-field-ip: IP-adres waarvandaan die aanmelding gekom het
webhook-internal-hosts-rejected: Nie 'n gasheer nie, nie gestoor nie:
activity-recovery-cancel-older-prompt: Kanselleer elke hangende kennisgewing van aktiwiteite ouer as hoeveel dae?
vcs-synced-from: Gesinkroniseer vanaf %s: maak dit daar oop en toe.
vcs-synced-issue: Hierdie kwessie is gesinkroniseer: maak dit in sy spoorder oop en toe.
sync-write-back: Skryf veranderinge terug na GitLab: titel, beskrywing, kommentaar, toemaak en heropen
email-bounces-description: Wat WeKan doen met e-pos wat terugkom: 'n verkeerd getikte adres, 'n vol posbus, 'n afwesigheidsantwoord, 'n strooiposklagte. Elke soort het sy eie aksies, wat uitgevoer word wanneer dit soveel keer teruggekom het.
email-bounces-action-stop-email: Hou op om die adres te e-pos
email-bounces-action-notify-inviter: Laat weet wie dit genooi het
email-bounces-category-hard-desc: Die adres bestaan nie: 'n tikfout, 'n geskrapte rekening, 'n onbekende domein.
email-bounces-category-soft-desc: Vir nou nie afgelewer nie: posbus vol, bediener besig. Net baie agtereenvolgens beteken iets.
email-bounces-category-auto-reply-desc: Afwesigheids-, vakansie- of kaartjiestelselantwoorde. Die e-pos is afgelewer.
email-bounces-category-complaint-desc: Die ontvanger het die e-pos as strooipos gemerk.
email-bounces-ses-description: Stuur in Amazon SES die Bounce- en Complaint-kennisgewings, en 'n ontvangsreël vir die adres waarvandaan WeKan stuur, na 'n SNS-onderwerp, en teken hierdie adres daarop in oor HTTPS:
email-bounces-ses-topics: SNS-onderwerp-ARN's om te aanvaar, een per reël
email-bounces-stopped-only: Slegs die adresse wat WeKan nie meer e-pos nie
email-bounces-clear-hint: Vergeet hierdie adres se terugstuurs en e-pos dit weer
email-bounces-providers-description: As WeKan deur een van hierdie dienste stuur, skakel dit aan, gee die diens hierdie webhook-adres vir sy terugstuur- en strooiposklagte-gebeurtenisse, en plak hier die sleutel waarmee dit hulle onderteken, of die wagwoord wat jy in die adres gesit het as https://user:password@… of ?secret=…
email-bounce-provider-secret-required: 'n Diens wat aangeskakel is, het sy ondertekeningsleutel of wagwoord nodig.
activity-pub-enabled: Publieke borde publiseer hul kaartaktiwiteit op die fediverse (ActivityPub)
activity-pub-desc: By verstek af. Wanneer dit aan is, kan elke publieke bord vanaf Mastodon en ander fediverse-bedieners gevolg word as @board-<id> by hierdie WeKan se adres, en nuwe kaartaktiwiteit bereik sy volgers. Dit is slegs-lees: niks wat 'n fediverse-bediener stuur, verander 'n bord nie, en privaat borde word nooit gepubliseer nie.
caldav-sync-desc: Plaas hierdie bord se kaartsperdatums in 'n kalender - Nextcloud Calendar of enige CalDAV-kalender. 'n Sperdatum wat in die kalender geskuif word, kom terug na die kaart. Gebruik 'n toepassingswagwoord, nie jou eie nie.
caldav-invalid-url: Die kalenderadres moet 'n http://- of https://-adres wees, sonder 'n gebruikersnaam of wagwoord daarin.
caldav-not-linked: Stoor eers 'n kalenderadres en skakel sinkronisasie aan.
webdav-storage-description: Stoor aanhangsels in 'n vouer op 'n WebDAV-bediener - Nextcloud Files, ownCloud of enige ander. Gebruik 'n toepassingswagwoord wat vir WeKan gemaak is. 'n Bediener op WeKan se eie netwerk kan hier gebruik word, aangesien slegs 'n werfadministrateur hierdie adres stel.
sqrl-desc: By verstek af. Wanneer dit aan is, bied die aanmeldbladsy SQRL aan, en lede voeg eers hul SQRL-identiteit by in Lede-instellings. SQRL vereis WeKan by 'n https://-adres.
sqrl-scan: Skandeer die kode met jou SQRL-toep, of maak jou SQRL-kliënt op hierdie toestel oop.
sqrl-expired: Hierdie SQRL-kode het verval. Begin weer.
sqrl-description: Meld aan met jou SQRL-identiteit in plaas van 'n wagwoord. Voeg dit een keer hier by met jou SQRL-kliënt; jy kan dit enige tyd hier verwyder.
sqrl-disabled-by-client: SQRL-aanmelding is vir hierdie rekening vanuit jou SQRL-kliënt gedeaktiveer. Aktiveer dit weer daar met jou reddingskode.
sqrl-only-on: Jou SQRL-kliënt het hierdie rekening aan SQRL gesluit: elke ander manier van aanmeld word geweier.
sqrl-hardlock-on: Jou SQRL-kliënt het hierdie rekening hard gesluit: wagwoordherstel en e-posverandering word geweier.
sqrl-only: Hierdie rekening meld slegs met SQRL aan.
sqrl-hardlock: Hierdie rekening is aan SQRL gesluit: dit kan op geen ander manier herstel of verander word nie.
windows-sso-failed: Aanmelding met Windows het misluk. Jou Windows-rekening word dalk nie hier toegelaat nie.
enrollment-password-instructions: Bevestig jou wagwoord om die opstelling te begin. Hierdie stap meld jou nie aan nie. Jy kan nie hier ’n aktiewe stawingsfaktor vervang nie.
enrollment-setup-denied: Die opstelling kan nie begin nie. Gaan jou aanmeldbesonderhede na en kyk of eenmalige kodes reeds geaktiveer is.
enrollment-code-instructions: Gebruik tydgebaseerde kodes: SHA1, ses syfers en ’n interval van 30 sekondes. Hou die sleutel geheim. Die opstelling verval ná vyf minute.
enrollment-confirmed-instructions: Die bevestigingskode is reeds gebruik. Wag dat jou stawingstoepassing ’n nuwe kode wys voordat jy aanmeld.
registration-first-admin: Die eerste rekening kry globale administrateurregte vir hierdie domein.
auth-too-many-attempts: Te veel aanmeldpogings. Probeer later weer.
enrollment-setup-failed: Die opstelling kon nie begin nie.
registration-global-admin-disabled: Rekeninge vir globale administrateurs word plaaslik geskep. Openbare registrasie is gedeaktiveer.
auth-session-create-failed: Die sessie kon nie geskep word nie.
registration-password-unavailable: Registrasie met ’n wagwoord is nie beskikbaar nie.
expedite-limit: Slegs een oop kaart van 'n raad kan op 'n slag Dringend wees.
list-policy-placeholder: Wanneer mag 'n kaart in hierdie lys kom, en wanneer is dit hier klaar?
commitment-point-hint: Vanaf hierdie lys word werk aan verbind; die lyste daarvoor is opsies.
person-wip-over: __user__ het __count__ oop kaarte; die WIP-limiet per persoon is __limit__.
feature-list-policies-desc: Elke lys se beleid - wanneer 'n kaart mag inkom en wanneer dit daar klaar is - by die lysopskrif. Per bord aangeskakel in Bordinstellings / Lys.
feature-commitment-point-desc: Die lys vanaf waar werk aan verbind word, gemerk by sy opskrif. Per bord gekies in Bordinstellings / Lys.
feature-person-wip-limit-desc: Hoeveel oop kaarte een persoon op 'n bord mag hou; 'n oopgemaakte kaart waarsku oor enigiemand daarbo. Per bord gestel in Bordinstellings / Lys.
feature-standup-timer-desc: Die bordkieslys se Daaglikse staanvergadering: die bord se lede in 'n geskommelde volgorde, elk met dieselfde tydblok. Per bord afgeskakel in sy Scrum-instellings.
feature-retrospective-board-desc: Die bordkieslys se Terugblikbord: 'n nuwe privaat bord met die lyste Begin doen, Hou op doen, Hou aan doen en Aksie-items. Per bord afgeskakel in sy Scrum-instellings.
show-split-lists: Laat toe dat lyste in Besig en Klaar verdeel word
split-done: Hier klaar, wag om aangetrek te word
feature-split-lists-desc: 'n Lys verdeel in Besig en Klaar: 'n kaart wat daar as klaar gemerk is, wag, verdof, om na die volgende lys getrek te word, en die lyskop tel albei. Per bord toegelaat in Bordinstellings / Lys, en dan in elke lys se kieslys aangeskakel.
workload-intro: Die beraamde ure en storiepunte van die kaarte wat aan elke persoon toegewys is, week vir week, teenoor die ure wat hulle het: hul werktyd, afwesighede en openbare vakansiedae. Klik op 'n week om sy kaarte te sien.
workload-truncated: Te veel om gelyktydig te wys: die verslag wys slegs die eerste persone en kaarte. Kies minder weke of minder borde.
workload-allocations-intro: Hoeveel van 'n persoon se tyd na 'n bord gaan, of watter rolle 'n bord nodig sal hê voordat iemand benoem is.
workload-invalid-estimate: Die beraming moet tussen 0 en 10000 ure wees.
feature-workload-desc: Die gebruikerskieslys se Werklading en kapasiteit: beraamde ure en storiepunte van elke persoon se kaarte, week vir week, teenoor hul werktyd, afwesighede en openbare vakansiedae, met toekennings aan borde en plekhouerrolle.
billing-intro: Die borde waarvan jy 'n admin is: hul begroting, wat hul werk gekos het en sal kos teen die uurtariewe wat jy stel, en fakture vir die ure wat bestee is. Slegs bord-admins sien dit.
billing-no-boards: Jy is nie 'n admin van enige bord nie.
billing-unrated: __hours__ h het geen uurtarief nie en is nie geprys nie. Stel 'n tarief vir die bord of vir daardie persone.
billing-nothing-to-invoice: Elke faktureerbare uur is reeds gefaktureer.
billing-set-rate-first: Stel eers 'n uurtarief vir hierdie bord.
feature-billing-desc: Die gebruikerskieslys se Begroting en fakturering: 'n bord se begroting in geld of ure, uurtariewe, die koste en voorspelling van sy werk, en fakture vir die faktureerbare ure wat bestee is. Slegs bord-admins sien dit.
billing-include-undated: Sluit tyd in wat aangeteken is voordat datums gehou is
billing-pay-by-scanning: Betaal deur te skandeer met jou bank- of betaalapp
billing-reverse-charge: Omgekeerde heffing: BTW word deur die koper betaal
billing-undated-included: Sluit __hours__ h in wat aangeteken is voordat datums gehou is.
billing-uncosted: __hours__ h het geen koste per uur nie en is nie in die koste ingesluit nie.
billing-bill-time: Faktureer tyd per uur (af: 'n vaste prys, slegs fooie en uitgawes word gefaktureer)
billing-approve-time: Keur tyd goed voordat dit gefaktureer word
billing-fees-intro: 'n Mylpaal of 'n vaste prys word een keer gefaktureer, vanaf sy dag; 'n voorskot elke maand vanaf sy dag tot sy einde.
billing-nothing-to-approve: Geen tyd wag op goedkeuring nie.
billing-unapproved: __hours__ h wag op goedkeuring en is nie op hierdie faktuur nie.
billing-quotes-intro: 'n Kwotasie prys die werk wat nog gedoen moet word - elke oop kaart se skatting minus die tyd bestee - en die fooie wat nog nie gefaktureer is nie.
billing-accept-sets-budget: Wanneer 'n kwotasie aanvaar word, word dit die bord se begroting
workload-utilization-title: Faktureerbare ure aangeteken teenoor die werktyd van hierdie weke
cloud-panel-settings-intro: Op die Cloud Panel-domein bestuur die SuperAdmin die kliënte se domeine, hul databasisse, die CloudFlare-DNS en die Caddy-roetes, en elke kliënt sien hul fakture en praat met die SuperAdmin. Die SuperAdmin is 'n bestaande WeKan-administrateur.
cloud-panel-cloudflare-target: Die adres waarna die domeine wys ('n IP-adres of 'n gasheernaam)
cloud-panel-dns-conflict: __name__ het reeds 'n __type__-rekord: dit word gelaat soos dit is.
cloud-panel-caddy-intro: Caddy stuur die Cloud Panel-domein en elke gedeelde domein na hierdie WeKan, en elke domein met sy eie databasis na sy eie WeKan-houer.
cloud-panel-caddy-upstream: Hierdie WeKan, soos Caddy dit bereik (host:port)
cloud-panel-customers: Kliënte wat hier aanmeld (gebruikersname of e-posadresse)
cloud-panel-import-files: __count__ aanhegsels: kopieer ook die lêers uit die ou WeKan se lêerberging.
cloud-admin-not-allowed: Cloud Admin is slegs by die adres wat die bediener se CLOUD-omgewingsveranderlike noem, vir sy Cloud-admins en vir die kliënte van die domeine wat dit lys.
cloud-allowed-addresses-desc: Die IPv4- en IPv6-adresse, en adresreekse soos 203.0.113.0/24, van waar 'n Cloud-admin mag aanmeld. Een per reël. Leeg: enige adres.
cloud-allowed-addresses-lockout: Jou adres __address__ is nie in hierdie lys nie. As dit gestoor word, sal jy uitgesluit word, daarom word dit nie gestoor nie.
admin-panel-allowed-addresses-desc: Die IPv4- en IPv6-adresse en adresreekse, een per reël, waarvandaan die Admin Paneel en die admin REST API gebruik kan word. Leeg: enige adres.
admin-panel-allowed-addresses-env: Die bediener se omgewingsveranderlike ADMIN_PANEL_ALLOWED_IP_ADDRESSES besluit in plaas van hierdie lys.
admin-panel-address-refused: Die Admin Paneel kan nie vanaf jou adres __address__ gebruik word nie.
website-view-empty: Niks is nog op hierdie webwerf gepubliseer nie.
feature-views-website-desc: Die bord as 'n webwerf: die kaarte van sy lys Published, die baan Pages as die kieslys en die ander kaarte as plasings, nuutste eerste, met hul aanhegsels. 'n Openbare bord kan daarin oopmaak, sodat besoekers die webwerf by die bord se adres sien.
feature-views-shop-desc: Die produkte op 'n bord se kaarte as 'n webwinkel: 'n kaart met 'n prys is 'n produk, sy etikette is die kategorieë, en 'n bestelling is 'n kaart in die Bestellings-lys. 'n Openbare bord kan daarin oopmaak, sodat besoekers by die bord se adres inkopies doen.
shop-decrement-stock: Neem bestelde produkte uit die voorraad
shop-sale-lists: Lyste te koop (niks gemerk nie: elke lys behalwe die Bestellings-lys)
shop-category-labels: Etikette wat as kategorieë gewys word (niks gemerk nie: elke etiket)
shop-orders-private: Bestellings word op 'n privaat bord geskryf, want 'n openbare bord wys elke kaart vir almal.
shop-show-on-public: Wys die Winkel in plaas van die openbare bord
shop-show-on-public-note: 'n Openbare bord maak in slegs een aansig oop. As die Winkel hier gekies word, vervang dit __view__ vir besoekers, en as Webwerf of 'n ander aansig in Bordinstellings / Bordaansig gekies word, vervang dit die Winkel.
shop-empty: Nog geen produkte nie. 'n Kaart met 'n prys in 'n lys te koop is 'n produk.
shop-accept-terms: Ek aanvaar die bepalings en voorwaardes
shop-privacy-note: Jou naam en kontakbesonderhede word op die bestelling geskryf sodat die winkel dit kan aflewer, en nêrens anders nie.
shop-price-changed: 'n Prys het verander. Kyk na die nuwe totaal en bestel weer.
shop-confirmation-email: Stuur die koper 'n bestellingbevestiging per e-pos
import-board-instruction-wordpress: Kies in WordPress Tools, Export, All content en Download Export File, en kies daardie .xml-lêer hier, of plak die teks. Squarespace, Wix en ander werwe wat 'n WordPress-lêer uitvoer werk op dieselfde manier. Elke bladsy en plasing word 'n kaart in die lys van sy status, bladsye in die baan Pages en plasings in Posts, met sy inhoud, kategorieë en etikette as etikette, en sy goedgekeurde kommentaar.
import-board-instruction-wordpressjson: Stoor die plasings en bladsye van die WordPress REST API (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts en /wp-json/wp/v2/pages) as een .json-lêer, en kies dit hier of plak dit. Elke bladsy en plasing word 'n kaart in die lys van sy status.
import-board-instruction-ghost: Kies in Ghost Settings, Labs, Export your content, en kies die .json-lêer hier of plak dit. Elke bladsy en plasing word 'n kaart in die lys van sy status, met sy etikette as etikette.
import-board-instruction-blogger: Kies in Blogger Settings, Back up content, en kies die .xml-lêer hier of plak die teks. Elke plasing en bladsy word 'n kaart, 'n konsep in die lys Draft, met sy etikette en kommentaar.
import-board-instruction-markdownsite: Zip die bronne van 'n Hugo-, Jekyll-, Eleventy-, Astro- of ander statiese werf - die Markdown-lêers met hul voorwerk, en hul beelde - en kies die .zip hier. Elke Markdown-lêer word 'n kaart: plasings uit die posts-vouers of met 'n datum in die lêernaam, die res bladsye, konsepte in die lys Draft, en die beelde wat dit gebruik as sy aanhegsels.
import-board-instruction-htmlsite: Zip 'n webwerf se lêers - sy .html-bladsye en beelde, soos gestoor met wget of HTTrack, of Medium se uitvoer - en kies die .zip hier. Elke bladsy word 'n kaart met sy hoofteks, en die beelde wat dit gebruik as sy aanhegsels; skripte, kieslyste en vorms word uitgelaat.
import-board-instruction-substack: Kies in Substack Settings, Exports, Create new export, en kies die afgelaaide .zip hier. Elke plasing word 'n kaart met sy teks, gepubliseer of konsep.
help-board-view-swimlanes-what-it-is-des: Swimlanes divide the board into horizontal bands, so each card belongs to both a list and a swimlane. A lane can stand for a team, a person, a customer or a kind of work, while the lists keep showing the stages of the work.
help-board-view-swimlanes-how-it-works-d: Click + in a swimlane header, or choose Add Swimlane in its menu, type a name and choose whether it goes above or below the selected lane. Pasting several lines can create one swimlane per line. Click a name to rename it, use the caret to collapse or expand a lane, drag its handle to reorder lanes, and drag its bottom edge to change its height unless a board admin has locked resizing.
help-board-view-lists-what-it-is-descrip: Lists are the columns that hold the cards. On a kanban board each list is a stage of the work, and a card moves from list to list as the work goes on. In Swimlanes view a list can belong to one swimlane.
help-board-view-lists-how-it-works-descr: Click the add list icon at the right end of a list header, or Add in the list menu, type a name and choose which list it comes after; pasting several lines can create one list per line. Click a list title to rename it, and the caret in its header collapses or expands it just for you. The list menu also has copy, move and archive, and you can drag the handle between lists to resize them when resizing is allowed.
help-board-view-table-what-it-is-descrip: The Table view shows the board's cards as a spreadsheet-like table, one row per card, with its list, swimlane, people, labels and dates. It is handy for scanning many cards at once and for adding or moving cards without dragging them across lists.
help-board-view-table-how-it-works-descr: Click a column header to sort, and click it again to reverse the order. Type in the search box to match card titles, lists, swimlanes and labels, and use Previous and Next to page through 25 rows at a time. The Edit button opens a card over the table. Wrap titles and Group by swimlane change the layout and are remembered in this browser. Archived cards are left out, and the sidebar Filter narrows the rows.
help-board-view-cal-what-it-is-descripti: The Calendar view places the board's cards on a calendar by their dates: a card with start and end dates as a bar between them, and its received, due and end dates as their own entries. Dated checklist items appear too.
help-board-view-cal-how-it-works-descrip: Use Today, Previous and Next to move around, and switch between day, week and month, each as a grid or a list. Drag a card to give it a new due date, or stretch it to change its end date. Click a day, or drag over hours in the week or day grid, to create a new card due then; it goes to the board's first swimlane and first list.
help-board-view-calendar-mode-what-it-is: Calendar Mode shows each card on the day of its due date, with its labels and full title, in a month or week grid. It is a read-only overview of what is due when, similar to the Trello calendar.
help-board-view-calendar-mode-how-it-wor: Use Today, Previous and Next to move by a month or a week, and Week or Month to switch the grid; the choice is remembered in this browser. Click a card to open it. Archived cards are left out and the sidebar Filter applies. To change dates by dragging, use the Calendar view instead.
help-board-view-multiboard-cal-what-it-i: Multi Board Calendar shows the dated cards of every board you are a member of in one calendar, so you can see everything due this week no matter which board it is on. Each entry starts with its board's title in brackets.
help-board-view-multiboard-cal-how-it-wo: Open it from the Board View menu of any board and wait until the cards of all your boards have loaded. Use Today, Previous and Next and the day, week and month views, each also as a list. Received, due and end dates get their own entries. Click an entry to open that card on its board. Dates cannot be dragged here.
help-board-view-time-what-it-is-descript: The Time view gathers the board's time tracking in one place: how much time has been spent, by whom and on which cards, and how much time is left until cards are due. Time is entered on the cards themselves; this view only reports it.
help-board-view-time-how-it-works-descri: Read the time spent summary at the top, then the breakdown by assignee and by card, with overtime cards marked. Below it every change to a card's recorded hours is listed by the person who made it. Click Export to save the report as PDF or Excel. Members who may only see cards assigned to them get the summary for their own cards, while the other sections stay empty.
help-board-view-timeline-what-it-is-desc: The Timeline view shows the board as it was at an earlier moment, using the board's history. It helps you see what changed and put a card back the way it was.
help-board-view-timeline-how-it-works-de: Click a point on the line to see each card as it was then, grouped by its list at that time, with its title, description, labels, members and due date. Click Now to return to the present. On a card, Restore to this state sets those values back after you confirm. Nothing is deleted: the restore is recorded as new history, and the button is shown only to people who may change that card.
help-board-view-stats-what-it-is-descrip: Statistics shows the board's status at a glance: how its cards are loaded and how many swimlanes, lists, cards, archived cards, labels, members and custom fields it has.
help-board-view-stats-how-it-works-descr: Open Statistics from the Overview group of the Board View menu and read the Board status table. Card loading tells whether this board loads only the visible cards or all cards, and whether that was chosen automatically for a big board. The counts are computed on the server, so they are right even on a large board. Any value can be selected and copied, and opening the view changes nothing.
help-board-view-group-by-assignee-what-i: Group by Assignee lists every card under the person it is assigned to, instead of under its list, so you can see who has what without opening each list. It suits a team meeting.
help-board-view-group-by-assignee-how-it: Open it from the Board View menu. Each assignee gets a section with their cards, the due date where one is set and a clock when a card is over time; cards without an assignee are under No assignee. Click a card title to open the card. The grouping uses the card's Assignee field, not its Members. People whose role only lets them see cards assigned to them get no data here.
help-board-view-gantt-what-it-is-descrip: The Gantt views draw the board's cards on a calendar so you can see what starts, what is due and what overlaps. Gantt is a table with one row per card and an icon for each of its dates, while Frappe Gantt and DHTMLX Gantt draw each card as a bar from start to end.
help-board-view-gantt-how-it-works-descr: Choose Gantt, Frappe Gantt or DHTMLX Gantt in the Calendar and time group of the Board View menu; cards need at least one received, start, due or end date. In Gantt, each week with dates gets its own table; click a card name to open the card or a date icon to edit that date. In Frappe Gantt and DHTMLX Gantt, members with write access can drag a bar to reschedule the card.
help-board-view-product-backlog-what-it-: The Product Backlog is the ordered list of work a Scrum team has not yet taken into a sprint. It shows the board's cards that have no current sprint, ordered by backlog rank, without moving them out of their lists.
help-board-view-product-backlog-how-it-w: Find a card in the table and, in its Actions cell, set its Sprint, Backlog rank, Release, Work item type and Acceptance criteria, then click Save. Smaller ranks come first. Hold Ctrl, or Cmd on a Mac, to put a card in several releases. Click a card title to open the card, and Show more to load the next 100 cards. Editing follows the usual card permissions.
help-board-view-sprints-what-it-is-descr: A sprint is a short, fixed period in which a Scrum team finishes a chosen set of work toward a goal. The Sprints view is where the board's sprints are planned, started, closed or cancelled, along with its releases and Scrum events.
help-board-view-sprints-how-it-works-des: A board admin first opens Scrum settings, turns on Scrum planning and chooses the estimate source, unit, completion policy and working days. Then create a planned sprint with a name, goal, start and end, assign cards to it from the Product Backlog, and click Start sprint. To finish, choose where unfinished work goes and click Close sprint, or give a reason and click Cancel sprint. Only board admins manage sprints.
help-board-view-sprint-report-what-it-is: A sprint report tells what happened in one closed sprint: what was committed, completed, added, removed and left unfinished. Velocity lists those results for every closed sprint, so the next sprint can be planned from what the team really did.
help-board-view-sprint-report-how-it-wor: In Sprint Report, choose a sprint and choose Cards or Estimate above the bars, then read the daily scope and remaining work and the change-by-change history below. In Velocity, read one row per closed sprint. Results come from snapshots taken when each sprint started and closed, so later estimate changes do not rewrite them. Export saves the results as PDF or Excel, and Refresh reloads the report.
help-board-view-burndown-what-it-is-desc: These Scrum charts show progress over time. Burndown shows how much work is left day by day and Burnup how much is done, Velocity shows how much each closed sprint completed, Release Burndown follows the work left in a release, and Epic Progress shows how far parent cards have come.
help-board-view-burndown-how-it-works-de: Choose the chart under Scrum in the Board View menu. Each draws from the board's own cards and sprints and shows the numbers in a table under the chart. Velocity needs at least one closed sprint, and lets you choose Cards or Estimate. Click Export at the top to save the same numbers as PDF or Excel. A chart with nothing to draw yet says No results.
help-board-view-roadmap-what-it-is-descr: The Roadmap groups cards into rows by the value of a custom field, such as a release or an epic, and draws each row's cards on a timeline. It is useful for a release or theme roadmap when that grouping is already kept in a custom field.
help-board-view-roadmap-how-it-works-des: The board needs at least one text or dropdown custom field. Choose the field in Group by at the top; each value gets its own small Gantt chart of its cards, and cards without a value are grouped under No value. Cards are placed by their dates, so give them start and due dates to see them on the timeline.
help-board-view-dashboard-what-it-is-des: These Overview charts answer how busy the board is and how its work is spread: Dashboard and Pulse summarize the board, Workload shows who has what, Distribution how cards are divided, Dependency Map how cards block or depend on each other, and Activity Heatmap when people work on the board.
help-board-view-dashboard-how-it-works-d: Choose a chart in the Overview group of the Board View menu. Each page draws the chart from the board's cards and history and shows the table of numbers behind it. Click Export at the top to save the same data as PDF or Excel. When there is nothing to draw yet, the chart says No results.
help-board-view-bigboard-what-it-is-desc: Bigboard stacks every board you are a member of on one scrollable page, each with its own lists and cards, so you can work on all your boards at once.
help-board-view-bigboard-how-it-works-de: Open Bigboard from the Board View menu and wait while every board's cards load. Each board section works like a normal board: drag cards between lists, open cards and edit lists. You can also drag a card into a list of another board on the page, which moves it to that board. Lists can only be dragged within their own board. Click a board's title to open it on its own.
help-board-view-flow-what-it-is-descript: The Kanban flow charts show how work moves through the board: cumulative flow, control and cycle time, lead time, flow efficiency, throughput, WIP, aging work, blockers, forecasts of when work will be done, process behavior and whether bigger estimates take longer. They help you find where work piles up and how long it really takes.
help-board-view-flow-how-it-works-descri: Choose a chart in the Kanban flow group of the Board View menu. Read the note under the title, which says how it measures, then the chart and the table under it. Some pages take settings, such as target cards and date for Monte Carlo Forecasts or the size field for Work Item Size vs. Cycle Time, applied with Apply. Export at the top saves the tables as PDF or Excel.
help-board-view-reports-what-it-is-descr: These reports show how work flows through the board week by week: cards created and finished, net flow, how long cards stay in each list, the average age of open cards, the weekly throughput and how often due dates are met.
help-board-view-reports-how-it-works-des: Choose a report in the Kanban flow group of the Board View menu: Created vs. Resolved, Net Flow, Time in List, Average Age, Throughput Run Chart or Due Date Performance. Each shows a chart and, under it, the table of numbers it is drawn from. Click Export at the top to save that table as PDF or Excel.
help-board-view-map-what-it-is-descripti: The Map view shows the board's cards as markers on an image the board admin uploads, such as a floor plan or site map. It suits work that happens in places, like rooms, machines or plots.
help-board-view-map-how-it-works-descrip: A board admin clicks Upload a map image and chooses a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file, and can remove it later without losing the card places. People who may change the board see the cards that are not on the map yet; drag one onto the image, or choose it and click where it belongs, and drag a marker to move it. A marker takes the colour of the card's first label, and clicking it opens the card.
help-board-view-email-what-it-is-descrip: The Email view shows the board as a mailbox: cards are the messages, lists are the folders and labels are the labels. You can write and answer email from the board's own address, so replies come back to the board as cards and comments.
help-board-view-email-how-it-works-descr: Click Inbox, Sent, All mail, a list or a label to choose what is shown, type in the search box to narrow the rows, and click a row to open the card, whose comments are the conversation. Compose writes a new email and the reply arrow answers one, sent from the board's address. The board must first receive email, turned on in the board's Notification Settings under Email to card.
help-board-view-chat-what-it-is-descript: The Chat view shows the board as a chat workspace: each card with a conversation is a channel and its comments are the messages. The channel tree covers every board you can see, with the number of messages you have not read.
help-board-view-chat-how-it-works-descri: Open a workspace and a board in Channels and click a card; it opens in the middle pane and its messages in the chat pane. Type a message and press Enter or click Send; Shift+Enter starts a new line. To start a conversation on a card with no messages, click Show all cards for that board and pick the card. The panes are mirrored for right-to-left languages.
help-board-view-version-control-what-it-: The Version Control view shows the board as a code repository's issue tracker: cards are issues, labels are labels, labels with a due date are milestones, comments are the conversation and attachments are the files. It also imports and syncs issues from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo.
help-board-view-version-control-how-it-w: Browse open and closed issues, filter by label or milestone, and open an issue to read and add to its conversation. A card counts as closed when it is archived or in a list such as Closed or Done. New issues become cards in the board's open list, and Close or Reopen moves the card between the open and closed lists. Everything is ordinary card data, so changes are kept in the board's history.
help-board-view-column-sets-what-it-is-d: Column sets let you arrange the same cards in extra ways, such as by priority, milestone or size, without moving any card out of its list. Each set has its own coloured columns.
help-board-view-column-sets-how-it-works: A board admin types a name in New column set and clicks Add, then adds columns with a name and colour. Choose a set at the top; every card is in one of its columns or in Not placed. Drag a card to another column to change its place in this set only; its list, swimlane, labels and members stay the same. Each card also shows small labels for its column in the other sets.
help-board-view-website-what-it-is-descr: The Website view shows the board as a website built from its own cards and attachments, for example a site imported from WordPress, Ghost, Blogger or a static site. A public board can open in this view, so visitors see the site at the board's address.
help-board-view-website-how-it-works-des: Cards in a list named Published are on the site, or every list's cards when there is no such list; archived cards never show. Cards in a swimlane named Pages form the menu, with subtasks as sub-pages, and the other cards are posts on the front page, newest first. A card's description is the page text and its attachments are its images and files. To use it as a public board's view, choose it in Board Settings / Board View.
help-board-view-shop-what-it-is-descript: The Shop view shows the products on the board's cards as a web shop, with pictures, prices, categories, a product page, a cart and a checkout. A card in a list on sale becomes a product when its price field has a number, and its labels become categories.
help-board-view-shop-how-it-works-descri: A board admin sets the shop up in Board Settings / Shop: the price, product code and stock fields, a private Orders list, the currency, VAT, payment methods, the lists on sale and the labels shown as categories, then ticks The shop is open. Shoppers filter by category, add products to the cart and check out. Each order becomes a new card in the Orders list, and the buyer gets a confirmation email.
help-sidebar-filter-what-it-is-descripti: The Filter shows only the cards that match what you choose, such as labels, members, assignees, dates, custom field values, card text or how long cards have been in a list. It changes no card and nobody's access, and a combination of filters can be saved under a name and used again.
help-sidebar-filter-how-it-works-descrip: Choose labels, people, dates or other conditions in the sidebar, and the board shows only the matching cards. Under Labels, OR matches any selected label and AND requires all of them; clicking a selected label again excludes it. Card text applies as you type. Closing the panel keeps the filter on until you clear it. Global Search, also here, finds cards across all your boards.
help-sidebar-search-what-it-is-descripti: Search finds the cards and lists of this board whose text contains what you type, and shows each card found on the board itself. On All Boards the same button narrows your list of boards by title.
help-sidebar-search-how-it-works-descrip: Type in the field and press Enter. The sidebar lists matching lists and cards, and the first card opens on the board with a counter under the field. Press Enter again for the next card or Shift+Enter for the previous one; the arrows do the same and wrap around. Click a card or list in the results to show it on the board, and click Search again to close the sidebar.
help-sidebar-multiselection-what-it-is-d: Multi-Selection lets you tick several cards and then do one thing to all of them at once: set a label or member, change the colour, move, copy or archive them. On All Boards it selects boards instead.
help-sidebar-multiselection-how-it-works: Turn on Multi-Selection in the board header, then tick the cards' checkboxes, or use Filter to selection in the Filter sidebar to select every card the filter shows. Choose an action in the sidebar, such as Set label for selection, Move selection or Move selection to Archive. Click Turn Multi-Selection off, the X beside the header button, when you are done. You need permission to change the board.
help-sidebar-custom-fields-what-it-is-de: Custom fields are the board's own extra fields for cards, such as a version, a budget, a customer, a checkbox or a choice from a list. A field is defined once for the board, and each card can hold its own value for it.
help-sidebar-custom-fields-how-it-works-: Click + to create a field, give it a name and a type (text, number, date, dropdown, multi-select dropdown, checkbox, currency or string template) and choose where it is shown: on the card, on the minicard, on new cards or on every card. The type cannot be changed later. Number and currency fields can show their sum at the top of each list. Card values are then filled in on the opened card.
help-sidebar-archives-what-it-is-descrip: The Archive holds the cards, lists and swimlanes that were moved to the Archive. Archiving hides something without losing it, so it can be restored later, while deleting removes it for good.
help-sidebar-archives-how-it-works-descr: Choose the Cards, Lists or Swimlanes tab and click Restore beside an item, or Restore all. A card may not be restorable while its list is archived or full under its WIP limit, and the Archive says so. Board admins also see Delete and Delete all, which cannot be undone. Archived boards are restored from the Archive page of All Boards instead.
help-sidebar-original-positions-what-it-: Original positions shows where each swimlane, list and card was put when it was made, and which of them have moved since. It is useful after a big rearrangement, or to see the title a card was created with.
help-sidebar-original-positions-how-it-w: Read the three groups, Swimlanes, Lists and Cards. Each item shows its current name, Moved when it is no longer where it was put, the place it was created in, its original title when that has changed, and when it was made. Click Refresh to read the board's history again. Items made before positions were recorded have no row.
help-sidebar-summary-what-it-is-descript: Summary is a standup report of what happened on the board, person by person, taken from the board's own records. It answers what each of us did in the last day or week, and what is overdue.
help-sidebar-summary-how-it-works-descri: Choose Last day or Last week. Each member who did something or has overdue cards gets groups for cards Done, Moved, Added and Commented, plus their Overdue cards, and each card opens from its link. Click Copy as text to copy the whole summary, ready to paste into a chat or an email.
help-sidebar-since-last-visit-what-it-is: Since your last visit lists what other people changed on this board since you last had it open: new cards, moves, comments, due date changes and members added. The menu entry shows the number of changes.
help-sidebar-since-last-visit-how-it-wor: Opening the board records your visit. Open this view to see the changes grouped by card, newest first, and click a row to open that card. Your own changes are not listed. An administrator can hide the feature in Admin Panel / Settings / Features.
help-board-visibility-what-it-is-descrip: Visibility decides who can see the board: only the people added to it (Private), every signed-in user of this WeKan (Signed-in users), or anybody with the link (Public). Editing stays with the board's members unless a board admin allows otherwise.
help-board-visibility-how-it-works-descr: A board admin clicks the visibility button in the board header and chooses Private, Signed-in users or Public; the current choice has a check mark and the button then shows the new setting. On a Signed-in users or Public board, when the administrator allows it, the admin can also tick Everyone signed in can edit. For other people the button only shows the setting.
help-board-watch-what-it-is-description: Watch sets how much you hear about this board: Watching notifies you of every change, Tracking only of changes to cards you created or are a member of, and Muted of nothing. The setting is your own; other members choose theirs.
help-board-watch-how-it-works-descriptio: Click the watch button in the board header and choose Watching, Tracking or Muted; your current level has a check mark and the button shows the new level. If the change is refused, a message says why and nothing changes. The button is hidden when an administrator has turned watching off.
help-board-sort-cards-what-it-is-descrip: Sort Cards changes the order cards are shown in inside each list: by due date, title, creation time, votes or the board's label order. It changes only what you see, and no card is moved.
help-board-sort-cards-how-it-works-descr: Click Sort Cards in the board header and choose an order; the cards in each list follow it and the button says Sort is on. Click the X beside it to remove the sort and return to the order the cards were dragged into. The choice is kept in your browser across reloads. For Label order, a board admin can change the label order with Move up and Move down when editing a label.
help-board-settings-what-it-is-descripti: Board Settings collects everything that is set for this one board: its rules, planning, colour and background, dates, views, swimlanes, lists and cards, export and import, notifications, webhooks and archive. Most entries are for board admins; your role and the site's settings decide which ones you see.
help-board-settings-how-it-works-descrip: Open the board's right sidebar with the hamburger menu and click Board Settings. Pick an entry and its own popup or page opens. The entries are grouped: rules first, then the board's look, then how it is drawn, then what goes in and out of it, and last the archive.
help-board-settings-color-what-it-is-des: Change color sets this board's own colour theme, which every member sees on this board. It is a way to tell boards apart at a glance. Only board admins can change it.
help-board-settings-color-how-it-works-d: Click a theme swatch; it is applied at once, with no Save button. For the flat and clear themes you can also pick your own colours with the colour wheels and check them in the preview. A colour you set for yourself in Member Settings still takes precedence over the board colour for you.
help-board-settings-announcement-what-it: A board announcement is a message a board admin writes for everyone on this board, shown in a bar above the board's lists. Use it for notes every member should see, such as a deadline or a change in how the board is used.
help-board-settings-announcement-how-it-: Write the text, up to 2000 characters of plain text, tick Show it to everyone on this board, and click Save. Members see the bar until they close it with its X, which hides it only for them. When the announcement is edited, it is shown again to everyone.
help-board-settings-background-what-it-i: A background image is a picture shown behind the board's lists, and also as the board's tile on the All Boards page. It can be an image address on the web or a picture uploaded and stored in WeKan.
help-board-settings-background-how-it-wo: Type an image address in Background Image URL and click Save, or use Remove Background Image to clear it. To store a picture, click Upload background image and choose a file; uploaded pictures are listed below, where clicking one makes it the board's background, and the icons download or delete it.
help-board-settings-date-what-it-is-desc: Date lets a board admin choose one date format for everyone on this board, instead of the format set for the whole site. The same popup has your own week number switch and, for board admins, calendar sync that puts the cards' due dates into a CalDAV calendar such as Nextcloud.
help-board-settings-date-how-it-works-de: Tick the board's Date Format, pick a format and click Save; untick it to follow the site setting again. A member's own enabled format in Member Settings still wins. Show week of year switches week numbers on or off for you at once. For calendar sync, enter the calendar address, user name and an app password, tick the sync box and Save.
help-board-settings-all-boards-what-it-i: All Boards Settings decides what this board's tile shows on the All Boards page, such as the card count of each list and the members' avatars. It also sets card aging, automatic archiving of untouched cards, and whether list widths are personal or shared.
help-board-settings-all-boards-how-it-wo: Tick or untick a row and it is saved at once. With card aging on, write three numbers of days after which cards fade in steps. For auto-archive, write how many days without activity a card may stay before it is archived, or leave it empty to turn that off. Templates are never archived.
help-board-settings-board-view-what-it-i: Board View chooses which views, such as Swimlanes, Lists, Table, Calendar, Gantt or the charts, are offered in this board's Board View menu, and which one the board opens in. It is set separately for when the board is public and when it is private.
help-board-settings-board-view-how-it-wo: The popup has one row per view and four checkboxes: the default view and the shown views for a public board, and the same two for a private board. Tick a view's Show box to offer it in the menu and its Default box to open the board in it.
help-board-settings-swimlane-what-it-is-: Swimlane holds the board-wide swimlane settings: whether swimlanes can be dragged, whether their height can be resized, whether all swimlanes share one row of list headers, and which Scrum fields a swimlane shows. WIP Limit Groups, shared work-in-progress limits over several lists, are also here.
help-board-settings-swimlane-how-it-work: Tick the boxes you want; the Draggable checkbox is in the table at the top. One shared list header row shows every swimlane with all of the board's lists under one header row that stays on top, without changing the lists. Click WIP Limit Groups at the bottom to add or edit shared limits.
help-board-settings-list-what-it-is-desc: List holds the board-wide list settings: whether lists can be dragged, whether their width can be resized, whether every list has the same width, and the Scrum field a list shows. It also turns on the Kanban flow policies: list policies, lists split into Doing and Done, a commitment point and a WIP limit per person.
help-board-settings-list-how-it-works-de: Tick the switches you need; the Draggable checkbox is in the table at the top. With resizing allowed, drag the handle between lists to change a width. A flow policy row appears only when that feature is turned on for the site, and once on, its details are set from each list's own menu.
help-board-settings-shop-what-it-is-desc: Shop turns the board's cards into a web shop shown in the Shop board view. A board admin chooses which custom fields are the price, product code and stock, which lists are on sale, which labels are categories, where orders are written and which payment methods are offered.
help-board-settings-shop-how-it-works-de: Set the rows and click Save; everything is saved together and checked again by the server. A card with a price in a list on sale becomes a product. Orders are written as cards to the Orders list, which must be on a private board, and the buyer can get a confirmation email. You can also make the Shop what visitors of the public board see.
help-board-settings-card-what-it-is-desc: Card decides what the minicards and the opened cards of this board show, and in what order, each independently. Use it when a board relies on a few fields, for example to put the description or the custom fields first, or to show the due date first on minicards.
help-board-settings-card-how-it-works-de: The popup has two panes, Show on Minicard and Show on Card. Tick or untick a section or a field to show or hide it, and drag rows to change their order. A few sections have their own menu with more settings, such as Subtasks and the card's dragging options.
help-board-settings-import-export-what-i: Export writes this board, or part of it, to a file: WeKan's own formats, spreadsheets, PDF, HTML, calendar files and the formats of many other tools. Import adds content from a WeKan export into this board. A board export is not a backup of the whole site.
help-board-settings-import-export-how-it: In Export, choose what to include first, then click a format and the file downloads. In Import, choose a WeKan export file in json or zip format and its content is added to this board. Import needs write access to the board, and either can be turned off by the site administrator.
help-board-settings-notifications-what-i: Notifications sets this board's defaults for email and in-app notifications, its due date reminders, email to card, and how notifications are delivered. A member's own explicit choice can still override the board default.
help-board-settings-notifications-how-it: For the in-app tray and email, pick Default to follow the site setting, or Yes or No to override it for this board. Under Due date reminders, write the days to remind on, separated by commas, where 0 is the due day and negative numbers are days after it, then click Save. The delivery sections below set what a notification carries, grouping and timing.
help-board-settings-webhooks-what-it-is-: Outgoing Webhooks send this board's activities to another service, such as a chat tool or your own integration, as they happen. Each webhook posts the activity's text together with the names and links of the board, list, swimlane, card and people involved.
help-board-settings-webhooks-how-it-work: Write a name, the address the receiving service gave you and, if it wants one, a token, choose the type and click Create. A saved webhook shows more options: which activities it sends, direct messages to card members for Mattermost, and how its messages are grouped and timed. Edit and Save it again, or use Disable This Webhook to stop it.
help-board-settings-scrum-meetings-what-: Two helpers for Scrum meetings, available to every member of the board. Daily standup is a timer that gives each member the same timebox, and Retrospective board makes a new board for a Start, Stop, Continue retrospective.
help-board-settings-scrum-meetings-how-i: Daily standup lists the board's members in a shuffled order; Start counts down the first person's time, which turns red when it runs over, and Next hands over until the last one. The timer runs only in your browser. Retrospective board creates and opens a new private board with the lists Start doing, Stop doing, Keep doing and Action items.
help-board-settings-wip-limit-groups-wha: A WIP limit group is one work-in-progress limit shared by two or more lists together, on top of each list's own limit. It is useful when work in progress spans several lists, such as Doing, Review and Testing, or when you want to cap a whole swimlane.
help-board-settings-wip-limit-groups-how: Under Add WIP limit group, tick the lists to count together, or choose a swimlane and click Apply to swimlane to tick its lists. Set the limit and click Add WIP limit group. An existing group can be changed with Apply, switched on or off with Enable WIP Limit, or removed with Delete.
help-board-settings-subtasks-what-it-is-: Subtasks split a big card into smaller cards that can each be assigned, scheduled and moved on their own, while the parent card lists them and counts how many are done. These settings decide where new subtasks are created and how a subtask shows its parent.
help-board-settings-subtasks-how-it-work: Choose how a subtask's minicard names its parent, whether the board's cards have the Subtasks section, and the board, list and swimlane new subtasks are created in. By default they go to a board of their own. Subtasks themselves are added from an opened card's Subtasks section.
help-rules-what-it-is-description: Rules automate the board: when something happens, the trigger, WeKan does something, the action. For example, when a card is moved to Done, mark it complete. Rules are made by board admins, and a board can let its members read them.
help-rules-how-it-works-description: Type a title, pick a trigger and fill in its fields, then pick an action; the rule is saved and runs from then on unless disabled. In the Workflow view you can build rules by dragging a trigger and an action. Rules can be renamed, deleted, exported and imported, and a rule can have more triggers and actions in its details.
help-member-settings-what-it-is-descript: Member Settings is your own menu, opened from your username or avatar at the top right. It has your own pages such as My Cards, Due Cards and Starred, the board overviews, and all your personal settings, from profile and password to language and fonts.
help-member-settings-how-it-works-descri: Click your username or avatar and pick an entry; its page or popup opens. What you see depends on your account type, your role and the site's settings. When a site administrator's feature profile hides some features for you, the menu says how many are hidden.
help-member-edit-profile-what-it-is-desc: Edit Profile changes how other people see you in WeKan: your full name and initials, and, when the site allows it, your username and email address. When the site allows it, you can also delete or anonymize your own account here.
help-member-edit-profile-how-it-works-de: Change the fields and click Save; the popup closes when it worked and shows the error otherwise. A username or email address already used by another account is refused, and a changed email address is marked unverified. Delete removes your account with no undo, while Anonymize account keeps your history but replaces your name.
help-member-change-settings-what-it-is-d: Change Settings holds your personal editing and display choices, such as drag handles, marking cards changed since you last opened them, the focus outline, saving editors with Enter, opening many cards at once and the checklist sound. They apply only to you, on every board.
help-member-change-settings-how-it-works: Click a switch to turn it on or off; a check mark shows it is on and it is saved at once. For Show cards count if list contains more than, type a number and click Save. Date format, week start and notifications have entries of their own in Member Settings.
help-member-change-color-what-it-is-desc: Change color sets your own colour theme for WeKan. It overrides the site theme everywhere and also the board's own colour on board pages, but only for you.
help-member-change-color-how-it-works-de: Click a theme swatch; it is applied at once. For the flat and clear themes you can choose your own colours with the colour wheels and see them in the preview. Choose Default theme to remove your choice and see the board's or the site's colours again.
help-member-change-font-what-it-is-descr: Font lets you choose the typeface, text size and text colour of the whole WeKan interface for yourself. It helps reading, for example with a larger size or a colour that suits your eyes.
help-member-change-font-how-it-works-des: Click Default or one of the font buttons; only fonts installed in your browser are offered. Choose a size and pick a text colour on the colour wheel, or click Remove to go back to the theme's colour. Changes apply at once and are saved to your profile, and the preview line shows the result.
help-member-change-avatar-what-it-is-des: Your avatar is the small picture shown for you on cards, in member lists, comments and the header. Change Avatar lets you upload pictures, choose which one is used, delete them, or go back to your initials.
help-member-change-avatar-how-it-works-d: Click Upload an avatar and pick an image; it is added to the list, and clicking its row makes it your avatar, marked with a check. Click Initials to show your initials instead. The trash icon deletes a picture after you confirm. The popup shows the size and file type limits when the site sets them.
help-member-change-password-what-it-is-d: Change Password replaces the password you sign in to WeKan with. It is for accounts with a WeKan password; accounts that sign in through another service change their password there.
help-member-change-password-how-it-works: Enter your current password, then the new password twice, and submit. The site may require a minimum length and refuse passwords that are too close to your username or email, or found in known data breaches. After the change every session of your account is signed out, and you sign in again with the new password.
help-member-passkeys-what-it-is-descript: A passkey lets you sign in with this device's fingerprint, face, screen lock or security key instead of your password. The passkey stays on your device and WeKan keeps only its public part.
help-member-passkeys-how-it-works-descri: Type a name such as My phone and click Add a passkey on this device, then confirm with your screen lock when the browser asks. Your passkeys are listed with their names and dates, and the trash icon removes one. If the browser cannot make passkeys, the popup says so.
help-member-sqrl-what-it-is-description: SQRL lets you sign in by scanning a QR code with a SQRL app, without a password. Here you add your SQRL identity to your account once, or remove it again.
help-member-sqrl-how-it-works-descriptio: Click Add my SQRL identity and a QR code appears. Scan it with a SQRL app, or click Open SQRL client for a client on this computer; the popup tells you when the identity was added, or if the code expired or failed. Remove my SQRL identity takes it off your account.
help-member-two-factor-what-it-is-descri: Two-factor authentication makes signing in ask for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone after your password, so a stolen password alone is not enough to get into your account.
help-member-two-factor-how-it-works-desc: Click Enable Two-Factor Authentication, then scan the QR code with an authenticator app or type the code shown under it into the app. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows and click Confirm and Enable. From then on signing in asks for a code, and the same popup can turn it off again unless your administrator requires it.
help-member-hidden-boards-what-it-is-des: Hidden boards lists the boards you left that you could still reach through a team, an organization or your email domain, so WeKan hid them for you instead. Leaving such a board does not change your team or organization membership.
help-member-hidden-boards-how-it-works-d: The popup shows one row per hidden board, or says there are none. Click Restore beside a board to bring it back to All Boards. This only takes it off your own hidden list; whether you may open the board is still decided by the board itself.
help-member-change-language-what-it-is-d: Change Language chooses the language of the WeKan interface for you. Your choice is saved to your profile, so it follows you to every browser. Until you choose, WeKan follows your browser's languages and falls back to English.
help-member-change-language-how-it-works: Languages are listed by their own names, with a flag, a region line for regional variants and a note for right-to-left languages; the current one has a check mark. Click a language and the interface switches at once.
help-member-invite-people-what-it-is-des: Invite People sends an email with an invitation code to people who do not have an account yet, so they can register while self-registration is off. It lets members of the organization's own email domain bring in colleagues without an administrator.
help-member-invite-people-how-it-works-d: Write the email addresses, one per line or separated by commas, tick the boards they should join when they register, and click Invite. The popup says whether the invitations were sent. You need a board role that may invite for every ticked board, and an address that already has an account stops the sending.
help-member-date-what-it-is-description: Date chooses how dates are written for you, such as year-month-day or day-month-year, with or without the time. Your own enabled format wins over the board's and the site's. The same popup sets the first day of the week and the calendar system.
help-member-date-how-it-works-descriptio: The top of the popup shows the site's and the current board's formats, so you can see what you would inherit. Tick Member Settings: Date Format and choose a format, set the week start and calendar system if you like, and click Save. Untick your format and save to follow the board or site again.
help-bookmarks-what-it-is-description: The star group in the header is your bookmarks menu: it keeps boards, other WeKan pages, and from their own menus swimlanes, lists and cards one click away. Your stars are yours alone.
help-bookmarks-how-it-works-description: Click the star to star or unstar the board or page you are on; the count shows how many you have. Click the caret or the count to open the list and click a row to go there, or See all starred items for the full Starred page. In All Boards / Starred you can unstar tiles and drag them to reorder.
help-card-similar-cards-what-it-is-descr: Similar cards lists the cards of this board whose title and description look most like this one, so a second copy of the same task is noticed before work is done twice. A very close match is marked Possible duplicate.
help-card-similar-cards-how-it-works-des: Up to five similar cards are shown here, each with the list it is in, and the heading counts them. Click one to open it. The comparison is plain text matching done by the server, without any AI service. The section can be hidden in Board Settings / Card, row Similar cards, Show on Card.
help-card-activities-what-it-is-descript: Activities is the card's own history feed: who created it, changed its title, added a label, moved it, wrote a comment or attached a file, and when. It answers what has happened to this card without asking anyone.
help-card-activities-how-it-works-descri: The newest events are listed in order, with titles, labels, comment excerpts and file names shown formatted the same way as on the card itself. Click a linked title to go to that card, list or board. A site admin can choose in Admin Panel / Settings / Security to show rich text as plain text or without clickable links.
help-card-labels-what-it-is-description: Labels are the board's coloured tags, used to group and filter cards by topic, priority or anything the team agrees on. A label can also have a due date of its own, which turns it into a lightweight milestone such as Sprint 1 or v2.0 for every card that carries it.
help-card-labels-how-it-works-descriptio: Click a label or the plus button to open the labels popup, then click labels to put them on the card or take them off; a check mark shows the chosen ones. The pencil beside a label edits its name, colour and due date, and a label with a due date shows that date next to it. Stickers and locations are in this same section.
help-card-dates-what-it-is-description: A card has four optional dates: Received for when the task arrived, Start for when work began, Due for the deadline and End for when it was finished. The due date badge is coloured by urgency and counts the days left, so late work stands out on the board.
help-card-dates-how-it-works-description: Click the plus beside a date, or the date's badge, pick the day and the time and save; a due date without a chosen time gets 17:00. Open the same popup again to change or delete it. With keyboard shortcuts on, pressing d on a card opens its due date. The card also counts how many times its due date has been changed.
help-card-members-what-it-is-description: The Members section says who is involved with the card: its members, its assignees, who created it, who requested the work and who assigned it. Requested By and Assigned By can hold board members and also a free text note, for example a name from another tracker.
help-card-members-how-it-works-descripti: Click the round plus in a row to open a list of board members and pick people; they are shown as avatars or initials, and clicking an avatar again removes them. Under Requested By and Assigned By, the Add link below the plus writes the free text instead. Which rows appear is chosen in Board Settings / Card.
help-card-fields-what-it-is-description: The Card section holds the card's own working fields, such as its dependencies, blocked state, class of service, priority scores, its sorting number and its card buttons. An opened card shows every field the board has chosen to show on cards, empty or not, ready to be filled in.
help-card-fields-how-it-works-descriptio: Fill in or change a field directly in this section. What appears here, in which section and in what order is decided for the whole board in Board Settings / Card, in the Show on Card pane: tick or untick a row, or drag it to reorder. The minicard follows the Show on Minicard pane the same way.
help-card-time-what-it-is-description: Time tracking records how many hours have been spent on the card, with an optional estimate, Billable and Overtime flags and a day by day log of who worked how long. The total feeds the board's time, workload and billing views, and the Flowtime and Pomodoro timers here add to it.
help-card-time-how-it-works-description: Click the time badge or the hamburger beside Spent time to open Change spent time, enter the hours (decimals allowed), optionally an estimate and the flags, and Save.
